---
title: "Teaching"
---

I believe every biologist can learn to code, and that the earlier it happens the better the science gets. Teaching computational skills to bench scientists has been a constant thread through my graduate work.

## IBS 519 — Statistical Rigor & Reproducibility

For several years I've helped teach this Emory course introducing incoming graduate students to R programming, statistics, and reproducible analysis. I've led hands-on TA sessions on topics from Unix fundamentals to loops and functional programming in R.

Materials from my sessions are on GitHub: [IBS519_TAsessions](https://github.com/jrose835/IBS519_TAsessions).

## GitHub for Scientists

A short, practical introduction to Git and GitHub aimed at scientists who code but have never version-controlled anything. Built for lab-mates; useful for anyone making the jump.

[GitHubForScientists on GitHub](https://github.com/jrose835/GitHubForScientists).
